title: Choose Mizan's new visual world
question: The roll assigned the Swiss information system. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Information System (Swiss / Aicher)
options.lineage: International Typographic Style information design: Otl Aicher's Munich '72 system, Swiss rail timetables
options.thesis: The semester as a strict information system: one grid, one hour scale, flat colour fields that code departments, huge numerals that state the cost.
options.viewport: Overview opens as a poster-scale sheet: gap hours as a huge numeral, the Sun–Thu hour scale across the full width, cohorts as flat coloured bars, 'Optimize semester' as a solid blue block.
options.risk: Can read cold or 'generic Swiss' if the colour coding is timid; needs full-strength colour and oversized numerals to land on a projector.

raised.raise: Decisions run as a numbered station strip: Preview → Propose → Approve → Publish, with the irreversible step marked.
Before/after metrics render as registered plates at identical scale so the change is directly comparable.
One time axis (08:00–18:00) rules every page: metrics, timetable and proposals share the same hour scale.
Every section carries a fixed label grid: code, course, cohort, room, seats.
One state vocabulary: selected = inverted (ink field, white type).

options.label: Registrar's Timetable Booklet
options.lineage: printed university course-schedule booklets and official approval stamps
options.thesis: Mizan as the registrar's printed schedule book: ledger-ruled pages, section codes in tabular columns, approvals as a red stamp.
options.viewport: A ruled booklet spread: the week's timetable as the printed page, gap cost in the margin, the approval stamp at the foot.
options.risk: Familiar; close to where most runs land for scheduling tools and can tip into nostalgia.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Each page is a junction: one saturated yellow band shows only the next decision, with monumental numbers.
options.viewport: A yellow band across the top: '4 proposals waiting → Review', gap hours monumental beneath it.
options.case: Strong on clarity (one decision at a time fits approve/publish); weaker audience identification for a university committee.
options.risk: Yellow everywhere can fight the dense timetable and tables.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: Amber safelight stations where results emerge slowly.
options.viewport: Amber stations from compose to dry.
options.case: Loses both axes: judges don't map scheduling to a darkroom; amber hurts data legibility.
options.kept: Numbered irreversible stations with a preview before commit.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: One subject tracked across fixed-scale plates.
options.case: Loses both axes: no audience link, cream-and-serif default.

options.label: Mesophotic Dive
options.thesis: A single vertical depth axis rules everything.
options.viewport: A depth profile with the active band lit.
options.case: Loses both axes: the metaphor distracts from the timetable.

options.label: Sneaker Box Archive
options.thesis: A wall of labelled boxes you pull out and open.
options.viewport: A stacked wall of end labels.
options.kept: A fixed label grid on every record.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.viewport: Overlapping windows on a dithered desktop.
options.case: Loses both axes: novelty over clarity, no colour coding for departments.
options.kept: Inversion as the one selection state.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished SaaS admin dashboard: sidebar, KPI cards, charts, tables.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar nav, four KPI cards, a chart and a recent-activity table.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other hackathon dashboard by design.
